title: My Love Letter To RPG Maker

posts.author: Indsh
posts.body:
The thought of this being a goodbye is bitter sweet and not what I was thinking about when i came to the forum to leave this post but when deciding what thread to post in it seemed like the only fitting one.
I am currently making a game for Nintendo Switch, I became an authorised Nintendo developer in 2018 but haven't put anything out yet, taking years to make anything seems to be one of my USP's.
I decided that from the 1st of Jan I will post 1 video a day on youtube everyday so that when my game is finished I am not trying to launched it into a complete vacuum, in that process one of my friends dm'd me and asked "Have you released that game?". The statement didn't make sense, it felt like a poke at the fact I have said I'm making a game before but never released it, but the truth is I had released the game he was talking about, it was the one I spent 5 years making in RPG maker and posted
quietly
with no fan fair.
The next morning needing fresh ideas for videos (preferably those to do with games/design) I made a video about making that game and posted the link prepping myself for this road of actually putting stuff out there. It felt great but I couldn't tell the whole story, I didn't really get to express how much RPG Maker has meant to me and my development.
I started my first company when I was 15 (in 2004 ) but what alot of people don't know is that company started because of RPG Maker. Me and the friend I created it with only made the name that would end up being the company name because we needed a title screen for games we were creating on RPG Maker. He would end up flying around the world dj'ing and I would be filming all the best rappers in my city...pretty cool stuff...but it all started with the light bulb moment when figuring out how switches work.
14 years later after not using the program for over a decade I would find myself back, this was because of the announcement of MV. At that point I had got my (different) business to a model where I was creating and teaching how to create comic books whilst getting people to sell them part time for a 50/50 split. MV being cross platform meant I could bring my characters to life in the way I had always dreamed. The only reason i stop using RPG Maker in the first place is because I was one of those toxic people who thought anyone using a Maker higher then RM2K3 was cheating by using plugins and code and so (naturally) as new Makers came out and became more popular, and the fact those makers were PC only and we had macs meant I faded my self out.  So as I tested (i think) XP in preparation for MV I fell in love with the plugins, I felt something shift but that toxic part of me made a new decree. "I will only ever use RPG Maker".
With that I had an ambitious goal, to make my own action battle system. I didn't know how to code but for some reason i though I could do it and some how I did. I will leave that part for the
video
.
Short story long is that the process taught me how to code, I when I learnt how to code I realised I love coding. Not only do I love coding but coding is actually my favorite thing. Perfect threshold between art and science, the connection between how most things are made and distributed.
When I was just involved in the creative side I had a University research me, by learning how to code I got the chance to do my own research, get grants funded on my own all the way to now where I am actually pioneering holographic games and a leading voice in my city on the implementations of AI. I never went to University but I have been paid more then 2 medical degrees worth of research grants genuinely all starting with this software.
Like I said this is not a goodbye and yet it kind of is, I don't plan on using the software again, I broke my promise. I used RPG Maker to level up to Unity and only plan to keep moving forward. I will always sing the praises of this software and this community. Genuinely this software should be in every school, I have taught using it and if I was still teaching young people I would use it again.
Talking of community there are so many individuals who take there time and effect hear it would be impossible to shout them all out but I have to shout out Galv. Galv was so gracious with his time, at that time I think I was only giving him $6 a month or something but he would answer all my questions. He was so creative with his code sparking ideas in my own head giving me the audacity to think I could manifest what was in my mind with this software, and code was so well written that as I read hes plugins that was 100% the beginning stages of me learning how to code so a big thank you to Galv. And got to shout out Yanfly cause that's everyone's big homie here! (literally same influence as Galv minus the messaging)
Yeah I feel like for now this is what I wanted to get out to this community, and as destiny has lead me to post this in the hello/goodbye thread I will say this to the new comers, welcome to this amazing world...the amazing world of creating amazing worlds, post your builds often and if you have the discipline create something small. If you want to learn to code you can but for you it might be something different, sound design, story writer, heck you might even be a bug finder. I don't know you but unironically I do believe in your dreams. Make them and share them.
Indsh aka Vince aka SouthBlessed

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body: I wish you the best of luck in whatever and wherever you end up working on projects!
